claim: FLARE trains a 6-layer, 8-head transformer encoder on generator token probabilities, embeddings, and syntactic token types to predict line-level suspiciousness, then searches top-k regions and selects by execution outcome.
scope_conditions: LiveCodeBench, BigCodeBench; Qwen3-8B, Qwen2.5-Coder-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, Llama-3.3-70B, GPT-4o-mini
quoted_support: we present Flare, an iterative framework with a lightweight diagnostic model that predicts line-level suspiciousness signals for bug localization and code refinement.

claim: FLARE (k=1) gains 1.72% to 7.42% absolute pass@1 over NL-Debugging; k=10 gives 8.50% average improvement over no candidate search; on LiveCodeBench Llama-3.3-70B goes from 46.86 (alone) to 64.57 (k=1) and 76.57 (k=10).
stance_target: L4: localized repair beats regeneration/self-critique baselines
quoted_support: Even without expanded search, Flare (k=1) still outperforms Self-Debugging and Self-Refine in all settings and surpasses NL-Debugging in 9 of the 10 settings.

stance_target: L4 calibrated per-requirement confidence not occupied by FLARE
